title: Name the architectural layer of every feature module

facts.note: feature_tree: a path under features/ or wagons/ — the only place this rule applies. Applicability depends on the path alone, not on any detector finding.
Test files and vendored/build directories are never scanned; a test/vendored/build path classifier excludes them.

fires: Any source module under a features/ or wagons/ tree — whether being written, moved, renamed or already present — is subject to the rule, whether or not a detector has run.

A source module under a feature tree whose path has no layer directory and whose basename is not a layer filename (note: source exception S033 literally conflicts with this case; recorded unresolved in audit/verifier_detail).
doesNotFire: Test files, or files in vendored/build directories.
Source files outside any features/ or wagons/ tree.
Bare npm specifiers (resolve outside the project graph; not layer-checked).

given: A source module lives inside a features/ or wagons/ tree
when: the module exists in the tree (standing obligation; applies whenever you write, move or rename it)
then: The module must name its architectural layer, either by a layer filename (domain.ts, application.ts, api.ts, …) or by living in a directory named for the layer, matching its actual responsibility.
prefer: Place the module in the layer that owns its responsibility, or name the file with that layer when the repo uses the filename form.
During GREEN: derive the layer from the responsibility the current behavior implements.
During GREEN: follow the nearest existing feature layout.
During GREEN: move or rename only the affected module when placement is wrong.
avoid: Choosing a layer merely to make another import rule pass.
unless: Test files and vendored/build directories are never scanned.
Source exception (verbatim): "A file carrying no layer segment is outside these rules rather than in violation of them."
why: A reader should know a file's role before opening it, and the layering rules need something to read. Both forms are accepted because a nested Bun repo is idiomatic.
evidence: bun_clean_architecture_detector reports no layer-naming finding for feature-tree modules (findings are verification evidence, not a precondition of the obligation).
Prove: the file's declared location or name matches its actual architectural responsibility.
Prove: the current behavioral acceptance passes.
verifier_detail: Flag a module under features/ or wagons/ whose path carries no layer directory AND whose basename is not a layer filename; either form satisfies the rule (layer_declaration).
Layer filenames include domain.ts, application.ts, api.ts, …; a directory named for the layer is equally accepted. A nested layout such as features/orders/domain/total.ts is compliant.
Skip test files and vendored/build directories entirely.
Source exception: bare npm specifiers resolve outside the project graph and are not layer-checked.

Source exception (verbatim): "A file carrying no layer segment is outside these rules rather than in violation of them." UNRESOLVED SOURCE CONFLICT: this literally conflicts with the summary, which flags exactly such feature-tree modules; the source does not say which rules 'these rules' means. Both are preserved as authored; activation is not claimed unambiguous for this case until authoritative resolution.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
Bun realization mirroring coder.convex.layer-naming; core obligation coder.backend.code-is-organized.

ADDED TO THE MIRROR, worth flagging: the Convex sibling accepts only the FILENAME form because its function tree is flat; a full-stack Bun repo commonly nests (features/orders/domain/total.ts), so accepting only filenames would refuse the idiomatic layout. This realization accepts BOTH. The obligation is unchanged.
